title: The Dark Arts of Skill Engineering — Paul Bakaus, Renaissance Geek (Impeccable)
talk_summary: Paul Bakaus describes lessons from building the Impeccable design skill, arguing that skills should be treated as harness engineering (scripts, hooks, sub-agents, routing) rather than long prompts. The transferable core is adversarial blind sub-agent review, deterministic linters combined with LLM judgment, script-emitted instructions that models follow better than prose, and unskippable gates for weaker models.

takeaways.technique: Blind adversarial sub-agents plus deterministic detector, synthesized by main thread
takeaways.what_they_do: Spawns two sub-agents that cannot see each other's work: one acts as a human-style design director, the other runs a deterministic linter and collects evidence; the main thread then synthesizes both into one balanced critique, avoiding the self-grading bias and the 'no issues found = great' failure.
takeaways.evidence_quote: Two blind opinions beat one confident guess.

takeaways.what_they_do: Every skill invocation runs a context script (context.mjs) that emits structured JSON to stdout telling the model exactly what to do next (missing config, update available, repo state); the speaker found models follow instructions from script output far more reliably than the same rule written in the skill prose.
takeaways.evidence_quote: when you put something out uh from the exit value uh from the standard out of a script uh somehow the model will follow it a lot uh more than before

takeaways.what_they_do: For models that compress or skip multi-step instructions (Codex/GPT), the skill defines explicit numbered gates and requires the model to log the result of every gate, forbidding compression; the speaker notes that if a gate can be skipped, the model will skip it.

takeaways.technique: Hooks as passive guardrails (pre-tool-use for weak models)
takeaways.what_they_do: Ships lint hooks that fire on every edit across harnesses; for weaker models uses pre-tool-use hooks that block the write entirely rather than post-hoc warnings the model may ignore, with per-file ignore rules to manage false positives.
takeaways.evidence_quote: passive guardrails beat a command no one remembers to run

takeaways.technique: Mixture-of-experts skill routing and per-model builds
takeaways.what_they_do: Instead of one giant skill with if/else, Impeccable routes to different MD files per sub-command and per register (brand vs product), and compiles harness/model-specific variants with substitution variables and model-specific overfitting-avoidance rules.
takeaways.evidence_quote: If you cram every everything into one skill, it kind of blurs them. The instruction following becomes not very good enough anymore.

takeaways.technique: Ablation testing of individual prompt lines plus LLM-as-user eval harness
takeaways.what_they_do: Every rule in the skill carries a unique XML tag; the eval harness removes one line at a time, reruns across all target models, and uses a deterministic detector to see whether the line actually changed outcomes; an LLM plays the user for interactive flows.
takeaways.evidence_quote: every line of impeccable is ablation tested. So I test every single line and see what it does across all models
